title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 121
description: Ten questions on Psalms 121: lifting up the eyes to the hills - Yahweh, maker of heaven and earth, is the keeper who never slumbers.

questions.text: To what does the psalmist lift up his eyes in verse 1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:1 says "I will lift up my eyes to the hills."

questions.text: Where does the psalmist's help come from?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:2 says "My help comes from Yahweh, who made heaven and earth."

answers.text: From the king's army and its many chariots
From his friends and his brothers
From Yahweh, who made heaven and earth
From his own strength and wisdom

questions.text: What will he not allow to be moved, according to verse 3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:3 says "He will not allow your foot to be moved."

questions.text: What will he who keeps Israel never do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:4 says he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

questions.text: Verse 4 calls him "he who keeps" whom?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:4 says "Behold, he who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep."

questions.text: On which side is Yahweh your shade?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:5 says "Yahweh is your shade on your right hand."

questions.text: Verse 6 says the sun will not harm you by day. What will not harm you by night?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:6 says "The sun will not harm you by day, nor the moon by night."

questions.text: Besides keeping you from all evil, what will Yahweh keep, according to verse 7?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:7 says "Yahweh will keep you from all evil. He will keep your soul."

questions.text: Which two things of yours will Yahweh keep, according to verse 8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:8 says "Yahweh will keep your going out and your coming in."

answers.text: Your going out and your coming in
Your sitting down and your rising up

questions.text: For how long will Yahweh keep you, according to the last verse?
questions.explanation: Psalms 121:8 says "from this time forward, and forever more."

answers.text: Until you grow old and gray
For seventy years and no more
From this time forward, and forever more
Only until the next harvest is in
